description: Detects the combination MITRE documents for patching a network device's own operating-system image in place: an anomalous image-file transfer over TFTP/SCP/FTP, an unauthorized boot-loader-parameter or startup-image-path change, and use of memory/debug commands that can alter OS instructions in memory. This is the exact technique used by SYNful Knock, the covert Cisco IOS implant first documented publicly in 2015 and still the canonical reference case for image-patching persistence on Cisco routers.

mitre_analytics.name: Detection Strategy for Patch System Image on Network Devices

required_log_sources: Cisco Firmware/Image Transfer and Boot Event Log

data_sources.name: Cisco IOS/ASA Command-Line Audit Log
data_sources.description: AAA command-accounting log of every CLI command executed on the device, keyed by user session -- requires 'aaa accounting commands' configured and forwarded via the TACACS+ server or device syslog.

data_sources.name: Cisco Running/Startup Configuration Change Log
data_sources.description: Configuration-diff or archive-config change record -- what changed, when, and by which account.

data_sources.name: Cisco Firmware/Image Transfer and Boot Event Log
data_sources.description: TFTP/FTP/SCP firmware-image transfer events plus boot-time image-load and integrity-check messages.

detection_logic: Hand-authored SPL grounded in MITRE ATT&CK Detection Analytic AN1293 for T1601.001 (Patch System Image). Detects the combination MITRE documents for patching a network device's own operating-system image in place: an anomalous image-file transfer over TFTP/SCP/FTP, an unauthorized boot-loader-parameter or startup-image-path change, and use of memory/debug commands that can alter OS instructions in memory. This is the exact technique used by SYNful Knock, the covert Cisco IOS implant first documented publicly in 2015 and still the canonical reference case for image-patching persistence on Cisco routers.
spl:
sourcetype=cisco:ios (cmd="copy tftp flash*" OR cmd="boot system*" OR cmd="debug memory*")
| transaction dvc user maxspan=30m
| where mvcount(cmd) >= 2
| lookup maintenance_windows dvc OUTPUT in_window
| where isnull(in_window) OR in_window=0
| table _time dvc user cmd
tuning_guidance: Adapt sourcetypes/field names to the specific Cisco TA or syslog-forwarding pipeline in use (e.g. Splunk Add-on for Cisco IOS, Cisco ASA/Firepower App). Populate the reference lookup table(s) this search depends on before deploying: maintenance_windows.
investigation_steps: Review the specific behavior this search targets: Defenders may observe adversary attempts to patch system images by monitoring for anomalous file transfers (TFTP, SCP, FTP) of image files, unauthorized CLI commands altering boot system variables, integrity check mismatches between running and baseline OS images, and runtime memory manipulation attempts. Suspicious sequences include uploading a new image, modifying boot parameters, and subsequent reload/reboot of the device. In-memory patching attempts may manifest as debug commands or boot loader manipulation inconsistent with normal administrative activity.
Pull the full command/session history for the device and account involved in the triggering event.
Confirm whether the activity matches an approved change ticket, maintenance window, or known administrative account.
Check for other impaired controls or cleared logs on the same device around the same time -- this behavior rarely occurs in isolation.
Escalate to network engineering to validate device integrity (image hash, ROMMON state) if compromise is suspected.
